# AD FS

## Single sign-on (SAML 2.0)

In the portal, choose **AD FS** under Enterprise SSO and **Start with AD FS**. Then, in AD FS:

1. In AD FS Management, under Actions, click Add Relying Party Trust, choose Claims aware, and click Start.
2. Choose "Import data about the relying party published online or on a local network" and enter our metadata URL below — or enter the data manually.
3. Entering it manually: select "Enable support for the SAML 2.0 WebSSO protocol" and enter our ACS URL, then add our entity ID as an identifier.
4. Choose an access control policy and finish the wizard.
5. In Edit Claim Issuance Policy, add a Send LDAP Attributes as Claims rule (E-Mail-Addresses → E-Mail Address) and a Transform an Incoming Claim rule (E-Mail Address → Name ID).
6. Send us your federation metadata URL: https://&lt;adfs-host&gt;/federationmetadata/2007-06/federationmetadata.xml.

### The values the portal shows

| AD FS field | Value |
|---|---|
| Federation metadata address (host name or URL) (Select Data Source) | The portal's SP metadata URL (`https://…/sso/saml/…/metadata`) |
| Relying party SAML 2.0 SSO service URL (Configure URL) | The portal's ACS URL (`https://…/sso/saml/…/acs`) |
| Relying party identifier (Configure Identifiers) | The portal's entity ID (`https://…/sso/saml/…`) |
| Outgoing claim type (Transform an Incoming Claim (from E-Mail Address)) | `Name ID` |

### What to bring back

Copy **https://&lt;adfs-host&gt;/federationmetadata/2007-06/federationmetadata.xml** and paste it into the portal's **Metadata URL or XML**.

The assertion must be signed, and must carry the person's email address as an attribute or as a NameID in the `emailAddress` format. See [Any SAML 2.0 provider](generic-saml.md) for the details.

AD FS's own guide: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/operations/create-a-relying-party-trust>.

Then verify your domain and turn single sign-on on in the portal: [Enterprise SSO](../sso.md).
